utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T. The Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we begin by taking today's appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner, Gerard Dobbyn, and Crispian Smith Case Manager for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours, Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, and Eugene O'Sullivan appearing for Stanisic Defence thing morning, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. On behalf of Zupljanin Defence, Dragan Krgovic, and Stephanie Cagnet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have been alerted that the Office of the Prosecution has a preliminary matter to raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's only in connection with the calling of this witness. May I say, straightaway, Mr. Dobbyn is calling the witness, but because I've had discussions with Mr. Zecevic about this matter, I'm raising it. As I indicated last week, we have prepared, as in all the other cases for this witness, a spreadsheet which contains as number of columns which Mr. Dobbyn will ask the witness to explain. It also includes columns, two because it's English and in B/C/S, of the witness's comments on the context of the intercepts. As you recall, I mentioned that last week when I dealt with the matter. Mr. Zecevic, however, on behalf of Stanisic, and I'm assuming that he's supported by Mr. Krgovic, has taken objection to some of the comments. And on reviewing them, I take the view that there is some force in the objections to some of the comments. Accordingly, what we propose to do is -- we can't, unfortunately, do it today, because although we tried yesterday to produce a version without comments, something went wrong with the file. For tomorrow there will be a version of this spreadsheet without the witness's comments on it. And that we will ask to have admitted. It's been, as I say, it's been done on all the other case, and it's the only way, effectively, of getting evidence about some 200 or so intercepts in without taking weeks and weeks and weeks. And I understand, if the columns which relate to the comments are removed, there is no objection from either accused to the admission of the spreadsheet. Should Your Honours also -- obviously what we'll be asking for after cross-examination in the normal fashion because this is a 92 ter witness, is the admission of the intercepts as such. But as far as the spreadsheet is concerned, that would also be admitted. So I hope that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suppose the basis of the Defence's objection is that the comments amount to witness giving evidence out of court and the -- if I understand you correctly, the way that we should then proceed is that the copy that you now have would be used today as a working document and notionally marked as an exhibit with the proper item coming in tomorrow when you cleaned it up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, it's not -- the objection is not to comments out of court, that happens all the time and hearsay is admissible; the objection is to the nature of some of the comments. And having reviewed, in the light of Mr. Zecevic's objection, some of those comments, as I said, I think there's some force in what he says. Although some of the comments are unobjectionable and they simply set out the context as such, some are his opinion, and there I do see the force of his objection. And rather than try and sort it out between the two types, we'd rather, for simplicity sake, remove the comments entirely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I suppose the Defence has no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, that is what we discussed with Ms. Korner before court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So if the -- we are ready, the usher will escort the witness into court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is being escorted in, I'd just like to point out that a new list of documents was circulated last night. I just want to make sure that everyone has received it. And the only changes were that two documents were actually removed from the list because they aren't actually on our 65 ter list. And these were the ones, the last two documents were listed as 65 ter number 1991 and 3544. So that's just those changes to the list of documents to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOBBYN
utterances.text: And sorry, Your Honours, I'm sorry to interrupt, it's just I'm asking that we go into closed session before the witness comes into the room.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, thanks for being reminded. So we go into closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 2nd day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.56 a.m.,
